name: Quantified conversion flow
reader_question: How much of the input quantity survives each conversion step, and where is it lost?
relationship: Stepwise conversion on one unit: each step's input equals its output plus its loss; heights are proportional to quantity.
use_when: Every step reports both its output and its loss on one unit
The honest alternative to a Sankey when the flows are actually quantified
avoid_when: Losses or outputs are not reported — use value-chain-measured
Flows branch to several destinations — use a table or sources-and-uses

data_contract.notes: Process name (on the connector) and the product it yields (column label)
out + loss must equal the previous quantity

units: One unit; rectangle height is proportional to quantity from zero. Loss percentages use the step's own input.

editable: Column rectangles, carried bands and loss stubs as native shapes and text
not_data_bound: Heights are computed from the fixture and are not data-bound; editing a quantity means resizing the shapes and labels

table_alternative: A step table with input, output, loss and loss share.
variations: Two parallel conversion routes as stacked panels
limitations: Linear chain only; no branching or recycling
Up to five steps across the slide width
Small losses draw as thin stubs; the printed value carries the precision

excluded_alternatives.reason: Unquantified ribbons imply flows and proportions the data may not support; this form keeps one scale and reconciles each step
Centring hides that every column shares a zero baseline
